source.title: On Leave-One-Out Conditional Mutual Information For Generalization
source.authors: M. Rammal; Alessandro Achille; Aditya Golatkar; S. Diggavi; Stefano Soatto

page_placements.theme: Bounds and stability guarantees depend on assumptions and construction

record.tranche_reason: The paper derives and evaluates leave-one-out conditional mutual information bounds for generalization. Its experiments do not test the claim versions’ memorization, architecture, optimizer, batch size, explicit regularization, model size, magnitude-aware sharpness, or memorized-example removal conditions.
record.gate_note: The reported ResNet-18 results measure train/test error and information bounds, and the text reports effects of dataset size and synthetic noise on bounds or test error. These do not test any listed version; cited prior work on flatness and generalization is not recorded as a result.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates leave-one-out information bounds, dataset-size effects, and synthetic output noise. It does not test any listed version. Section 4.5 connects a bound to Hessian flatness, but neither measures magnitude-aware sharpness nor compares its ranking of generalization gaps with other measures. Removing individual samples to estimate stability does not test removal of highly memorized examples against random-removal controls.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors derive computable leave-one-out conditional mutual information bounds connected to cross-validation, optimization stability, and loss geometry. Their experiments obtain non-vacuous functional bounds and vacuous weight-based bounds. The computed bounds use synthetic randomization; applying them to the original deterministic algorithm requires additional assumptions or corrections.
record.recipe_differences: The paper develops and evaluates information-theoretic bounds rather than testing the listed interventions or measurements. Its experiments fine-tune an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-18 on image-classification datasets and add synthetic Gaussian noise to obtain bounds.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset size and synthetic noise variance affect the reported bound; increasing noise variance also increases test error.

fits_no_version.finding: For MIT-67 and Oxford Pets, weight-based bounds are 9.65 and 8.51, while prediction-based bounds are 0.493 and 0.514; the authors describe the former as vacuous and the latter as non-vacuous.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Functional leave-one-out conditional mutual information yields non-vacuous generalization bounds for the tested fine-tuned classifiers where weight-based bounds are vacuous.

fits_no_version.finding: Larger training subsets produce tighter functional information bounds.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The evaluated functional leave-one-out information bound improves as training-set size increases.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing Gaussian prediction noise lowers the functional information bound while increasing the noisy model's test error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Synthetic prediction noise creates a trade-off between a tighter information bound and predictive accuracy.

record.problems: Experiments remove only 10 samples one at a time across 3 random seeds. The dataset-size and noise-sweep outcomes are presented in figures without numerical values in the text. The stated experiment setup covers fine-tuned ResNet-18 models on image-classification tasks, not the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance under matched natural-label and random-label training.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers, local connectivity, and transferred initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizers and the effects of tuning or optimizer modifications.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout interventions, small-data regimes, and removal of dropout with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization gaps across networks and comparison with norm- and margin-based rankings.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and comparing retrained test accuracy.

record.verdict_notes: The paper's qualitative discussion of Hessian flatness does not test V7's magnitude-aware sharpness correlation. No supplied claim version receives a verdict.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fit and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
Test error as network width increases beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD on held-out benchmarks.
Large versus small batch training under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout’s effect on held-out error and the effects of removing dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness as a measure that tracks the training-test gap across networks.
Removing highly memorized training examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.
